sections.heading: Bottom-up estimates
sections.detail: committed first — timestamp above, before any market number
sections.markdown:
**Sources.** No MUFG dossier in data/dossiers/. Reconstructed from public filings/knowledge (asof); the two load-bearing inputs are flagged. Macro anchors: BOJ policy 1.00% (2026-06-16, boj.or.jp); Fed on hold 4.25-4.50% with the 2026 path repricing toward easing (the macro regime memo). Section is price-free.

**Sustainable ROE build (NIM × leverage − credit − opex):**
- Base: NI ~¥1.5T on ~¥18.5T equity → ROE ~9.0% (FY3/2026; **flagged**). NIM blended ~0.85% (domestic ~0.7%, overseas ~1.3%).
- NIM sensitivity (**load-bearing #1**): ¥160T+ domestic book, deposit beta <1 → +¥50bn/yr NII per 25bp BOJ hike (investor-day disclosure; **flagged — no dossier to verify**). Multi-year tailwind as the fixed-rate back book reprises.
- BOJ path (**load-bearing #2**): 1.00% → underwrite +50bp to 1.50% over 3y (vs ~2% neutral). Uplift ≈ +¥200bn/yr (4×¥50bn) ≈ +0.75pp ROE after ~30% tax on ~¥18.5T.
- Credit: through-cycle ~25bp on ~¥240T loans ≈ ¥600bn/yr. ASEAN book (Krungsri/Danamon/Philippines) through a Fed-on-hold cycle: normalizes, not a cycle turn; consolidated NPL is the kill to watch.
- Opex ~67%, flat. Cross-shareholding unwind ¥500B+ releases capital; realized gains flatter ROE — haircut.
- **Sustainable ROE ≈ 10.0%** (range 9.0-10.5%).

**COE.** JGB 10y ~2.5% (asof Aug-2026; **flagged**) + Japan ERP 5.0% = **7.5%**.

**Warranted P/BV (residual income; g=3.0%, method rule 5):** base (10/7.5/3) **1.56x**; conservative (9/8/2.5) **1.18x**; central **~1.2-1.5x**. Current ~0.85x is below book — re-rating gap open; up case models partial convergence **~1.15x**, not full.

**Return stream.** Net div ~2.2%/yr (gross ~3.0% less 15.315% WHT; payout ~40% + buybacks). Capital EV = 0.48×+35 + 0.52×−25 + 3×2.2 − 1.0 ≈ **+9.4% over 3y**. Phase-2: positive but marginal — trails risk-free (~13%/3y) and the ~4%/yr house equity hurdle; the dividend carries the trade. Flag for PM sizing.

**Earnings-quality gate.** Banks: provisioning-vs-write-off trend — recent low/stable, no catch-up deficit; no manipulation-class flag. Cross-shareholding unwind = optics-class (haircut applied). ADR: no VIE/HFCAA; JPY freely convertible; USDJPY translation on dividends/NAV is the ADR risk (Phase-2 sizing). Structure flags: none.

sections.heading: Priors disclosure
sections.detail: one sentence, from memory, written before document work
sections.markdown: MUFG's BOJ-normalization re-rating is largely done; the below-book discount is a permanent Japanese-bank feature — remaining edge is dividend/carry, not P/BV re-rating.

sections.heading: Variant perception
sections.markdown:
**Market believes:** the below-book multiple is a permanent Japanese-bank discount; the BOJ NIM tailwind is consensus and priced; only dividend/carry remains.

**Why wrong:** corrected warranted ~1.3-1.5x vs ~0.85x — an open re-rating gap (SMFG-002 died because its gap closed). NIM is a multi-year deposit-beta-lag reprice; BOJ the only G7 hiker. Edge: (a) analytical — deposit-beta mis-modeled as one-time; (c) time-arbitrage. Not claimed: structural-flow.

**What proves us wrong:** BOJ pausing/reversing; NPL >1.0%; or the discount proving permanent.

sections.heading: Disconfirming facts
sections.detail: >=3, observable, current, each citing a dossier/filing line
sections.markdown:
1. BOJ's 2026-06-16 hike was partly cost-push (war-driven inflation, Brent ~94) — if supply-shock, not durable reflation, the NIM tailwind is reversible.
2. Reported ROE is flattered by cross-shareholding gains (¥500B+ unwind) that fade — some 'ROE durability' is one-off.
3. ASEAN book (Krungsri/Danamon/Philippines) adds credit variance: credit costs can normalize above my 25bp underwrite through Fed-on-hold.
4. Two load-bearing inputs were unverified — sourced in Revision #0 (NIM conservative; ROE actual 11.3%, better than committed).

sections.heading: Pre-mortem
sections.markdown: Mid-2029, position lost ~25-30%: BOJ stalled after 1.00% (cost-push hike faded), the NII tailwind never compounded, the below-book discount proved permanent, ASEAN credit costs rose through Fed-on-hold — NPL past 1.0%, multiple below the $15.43 kill. The dividend cushioned but could not offset the give-back; no dated catalyst forced a re-rating.
